records.title: Closing all the branches
records.review:
As a long-standing NatWest customer working in the City of London, I find the continuing closure of branches deeply disappointing.

NatWest has now closed the Fenchurch Street, Liverpool Street and Bank branches, leaving one of the world’s largest financial centres with virtually no convenient face-to-face banking for the thousands of people who work here every day.

What is particularly frustrating is that the Fenchurch Street branch was refurbished at significant cost before being closed. That seems like a poor use of customers’ money.

Digital banking works for many day-to-day transactions, but businesses and individuals still need access to physical branches for more complex banking, cash services and personal advice. Removing so many branches from the City sends a message that loyal customers are no longer valued.

I hope NatWest reconsiders its branch strategy and recognises that the City of London remains one of the UK’s most important commercial and financial districts.
